title: Change vacancy/dues notification check interval from hourly to every 3 hours
description:
WorkScheduler.kt currently schedules both VacancyCheckWorker and DuesReminderWorker (the two periodic workers that produce warden-facing notifications - vacancy nudges and dues/overdue reminders) at `PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder<...>(1, TimeUnit.HOURS)`. Change both to a 3-hour interval so relevant notifications are still checked daily but less frequently/intrusively than every hour.

WorkScheduler.kt already has precedent for changing a periodic interval on an existing install: the comment above scheduleVacancyCheck/scheduleDuesReminder notes they must use `ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE`, not `KEEP`, specifically because a period change needs to actually take effect on phones that already have the old interval enqueued - the same care applies here, going from 1 hour to 3 hours.

InvoiceGenerationWorker and AutoBackupWorker are already daily (1 TimeUnit.DAYS) and aren't notification-cadence workers in the same sense - out of scope unless the user meant those too.
acceptanceCriteria: VacancyCheckWorker and DuesReminderWorker are scheduled at a 3-hour interval instead of 1-hour
Existing installs already running the 1-hour schedule actually pick up the new 3-hour interval (verify ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE is used, not KEEP)
No change to what triggers a notification (thresholds, overdue logic) - only how often the check runs
Confirmed on-device or via WorkManager test infrastructure that the new interval is what's actually enqueued, not just what the code says

history.note: "all thr relevant notifications should come daily at every 3 hrs interval." Confirmed in WorkScheduler.kt: VacancyCheckWorker and DuesReminderWorker currently both run hourly (1 TimeUnit.HOURS) - scoped this ticket to those two since they're the notification-producing periodic workers; InvoiceGenerationWorker/AutoBackupWorker are already daily and not notification-cadence in the same sense.

"For Lodgy-104 if the schedule is hourly, then no need to make it 3 hours." Existing hourly schedule is already at least as frequent as the 3-hour ask - no code change needed. Closing with no work done; kept on the board as a record of the decision rather than deleted.
